items.text: Back to the Future opened in American theaters on July 3, 1985, and became the highest-grossing film of 1985 in the United States.
items.question: Who did you go to see Back to the Future with, and where was the theater?
items.source_quote: July 3 – Back to the Future opens in American theaters and ends up being the highest-grossing film of 1985 in the United States, and the first film in the successful franchise.

items.text: On July 13, 1985, the Live Aid pop concerts in Philadelphia and London raised money for famine relief in Ethiopia.
items.question: Where were you when Live Aid was on television, and who watched it with you?
source_quote: Live Aid pop concerts in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and London raise over £50,000,000 for famine relief in Ethiopia.

items.text: "We Are the World" by USA for Africa spent four weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, tied for the longest run of 1985.
items.question: Where were you living when "We Are the World" was on the radio, and which of the singers could you pick out?
source_quote: These are the Billboard Hot 100 number-one hits of 1985.
The two longest running number-one singles of 1985 are "We Are the World" by USA for Africa and "Say You, Say Me" by Lionel Richie which each logged four weeks at number-one.

items.text: The Nintendo Entertainment System was released in U.S. stores on October 18, 1985.
items.question: Who was the first person you knew to have a Nintendo, and which game did everyone play?
items.source_quote: October 18 – The Nintendo Entertainment System is released in U.S. stores.
